intro: VRML to STL converts VRML models to STL on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to print on a filament or resin printer a VRML model made for colour. STL is the format every slicer reads: it only stores triangles, with no units or colours.

VRML (.wrl) is the classic 3D scene format and the one many full-colour 3D printing services ask for, because it stores a colour per face. VRML uses the Y axis up, as its specification says, and 3D printing uses Z: the model is turned so it stands upright in the slicer, unless you tick “Keep the original axes”. VRML stores no units: it is taken as millimetres and you can choose others.

Parts are read with their transforms, DEF and USE copies (each copy counts), per-face or per-vertex colours and each material's colour; textures, Inline files and PROTOs are not loaded. You can apply a scale and keep the VRML parts separate, merge them or get one per file in a ZIP.

The VRML geometry is not simplified or repaired on its way to STL. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, and up to ten files per task. Each file is converted in an isolated process on our server in the European Union and deleted when it expires.
steps: Upload one or more VRML files.
Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.

faq.q: Why does the STL come out lying down?
faq.a: Because VRML and STL do not use the same vertical axis. Tick or untick “Keep the original axes” in the advanced options.
Yes when the STL supports them (VRML, X3D and USDZ); STL stores no colours and the note says so.

faq.q: What if the VRML has textures?
faq.a: VRML textures are not converted: the geometry and each face's or material's colour go through.
